subject.title: Feature Request: Enforce skill execution sandbox when enabled: false

question: Should `skills.entries.<key>.enabled: false` become a hard read/exec access boundary for that skill directory, or should hard isolation require a separate strict skill-access policy?
rationale: The issue changes a public configuration meaning from visibility/eligibility to security enforcement and crosses filesystem, exec, sandbox, UI, docs, and compatibility boundaries.

options.title: Make disabled skills hard-denied
options.body: Treat `enabled: false` as a security boundary and add centralized enforcement plus upgrade/docs coverage for read, write/edit/apply_patch, exec, and sandbox materialization.

options.title: Add separate strict isolation policy
options.body: Keep `enabled: false` as visibility-only compatibility behavior and introduce an explicit security setting for deployments that need hard skill-directory isolation.

options.title: Defer to filesystem sandboxing work
options.body: Keep this issue open but make broader filesystem-root or sandbox policy the canonical implementation path, with this issue as a required acceptance case.

recommendation.title: Make disabled skills hard-denied
recommendation.body: Treat `enabled: false` as a security boundary and add centralized enforcement plus upgrade/docs coverage for read, write/edit/apply_patch, exec, and sandbox materialization.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is recent skill security and install-gate work, and the decision is primarily a security-boundary/product-contract call.
